question: Why do people who binge watch at night sleep worse, beyond simply going to bed later?
answer: Because their minds stay switched on. Exelmans and Van den Bulck surveyed 423 young adults: binge viewers reported poorer sleep, more fatigue and more insomnia, and the link ran through pre-sleep arousal, a racing mind at lights out. A story built to make the next episode irresistible keeps working after the screen goes dark.
move: What keeps you watching also keeps you thinking once you stop.
ask: What do I do in the last hour before bed that leaves my mind still running?
reference: Liese Exelmans and Jan Van den Bulck, Binge Viewing, Sleep, and the Role of Pre-Sleep Arousal, Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 2017
